h1: ZoomInfo alternatives for a small sales team on HubSpot
dek: Four contact-data tools a small team can weigh before it signs a ZoomInfo quote.
Every price and integration detail below comes from the vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This page is for a small sales team, roughly five reps, that runs HubSpot as its CRM and needs emails and phone numbers for prospects. You looked at ZoomInfo, saw a form instead of a price, and want to know what else is out there before you book a sales call. On ZoomInfo's pricing page, pricing comes through a sales form, with no public price.
If you have an enterprise data budget and a RevOps team to run it, this page isn't for you. It's for teams where the person who buys the tool is also the person who has to get it talking to HubSpot.

Start with Apollo if you want prospecting and HubSpot sync in one place. Start with Lusha if you mostly need contact details for a few reps and want to see the price before you talk to anyone. Seamless.AI and Cognism both work with HubSpot too, but you'll get a quote instead of a price tag.

Whichever you pick, check one thing first: who on your team is allowed to connect apps to HubSpot. All four name an admin or permission requirement for the HubSpot connection, and that's the step that stalls small teams.

Apollo has a free plan that stays free with no time limit. Paid plans on Apollo's pricing page: Basic at $49 a month on monthly billing and Professional at $99 a month on monthly billing. Two terms to know before you buy: all seats on an Apollo account are on the same plan, and unused credits expire at the end of each billing cycle.

On HubSpot, Apollo offers two-way sync of contacts, accounts, and deals, with emails, calls, meetings, tasks, and notes pushed to HubSpot. Per Apollo's HubSpot page, the HubSpot integration requires a paid Apollo subscription, and its help article says connecting it takes a HubSpot super admin. You also get 6 hours after enabling to set sync rules before anything syncs.

Lusha has a Free plan with up to 40 credits a month, CRM integrations included. Its pricing page lists Starter at $49.90 a month billed monthly, with 400 credits a month, or $37.45 a month billed annually ($449.10 a year). Professional is $69.90 a month billed monthly, with 600 credits a month. Credits work like this: 1 credit to reveal an email and 5 credits to reveal a phone number. Self-serve has a ceiling: teams larger than 5 users go through sales.

On HubSpot, Lusha pushes contacts and companies into HubSpot with field mapping, and checks for existing records first so you don't create duplicates. The catch for a small team: setup needs admin access on both Lusha and HubSpot.

Seamless.AI offers a free plan with 50 credits and no credit card. After that, paid plans are quoted per company, with no fixed public price. Its help center lists credit allowances by license instead: 250 credits per user per month on a Basic license, or 10,000 credits per user per month on a Pro license. Credit cost per contact: 1 credit for an email, 5 for a phone number, or 6 for the full contact.

On HubSpot, Seamless.AI imports contacts and companies into HubSpot one at a time, in bulk, or automatically when you save them. One permission matters: every user who connects needs App Marketplace Access in HubSpot.

Cognism sells Standard and Pro prospecting packages, each with 5 seats included. Cognism is priced by quote, with no public price. Credits are simple: 1 credit = 1 revealed contact, and there's no charge for viewing contacts you already revealed.

On HubSpot, Cognism exports contacts and companies to HubSpot with field mapping and per-field update rules, set up by a Cognism admin. I don't have an affiliate link for Cognism, so the button goes straight to its site.
If you need to see a price before you talk to a salesperson, you're down to Apollo and Lusha. Those are the two here with self-serve prices on the page.

If HubSpot is your system of record and you want activity to land there too, Apollo is the one of these four whose HubSpot page describes two-way sync with activities. The other three push contacts and companies into HubSpot.

If nobody on your team has admin rights in HubSpot, sort that out before you start a trial. Each of these tools names an admin or permission requirement for the HubSpot connection, and a trial clock runs while you wait for access.

faq.q: Is there a free ZoomInfo alternative?
faq.a: Apollo, Lusha, and Seamless.AI all have free plans. Apollo has a free plan that stays free with no time limit. Lusha has a Free plan with up to 40 credits a month, CRM integrations included. Seamless.AI offers a free plan with 50 credits and no credit card.

faq.q: Which ZoomInfo alternative syncs best with HubSpot?
faq.a: Of these four, Apollo describes the deepest HubSpot connection: two-way sync of contacts, accounts, and deals, with emails, calls, meetings, tasks, and notes pushed to HubSpot. Note that the HubSpot integration requires a paid Apollo subscription.

closing: For a small HubSpot team, start with the tool whose price you can see and whose HubSpot connection you can actually authorize.

products.name: Apollo
products.pick: Best fit if you want one tool for finding contacts and writing them back to HubSpot.

products.name: Lusha
products.pick: Best fit if a few reps need emails and direct dials at a price you can see before you call sales.

products.name: Seamless.AI
products.pick: Worth a look if you want a large monthly credit allowance and don't mind a quoted price.

products.name: Cognism
products.pick: Worth a look if you want a sales-led contract with seats bundled in.
